pages.title: Support agent overview
pages.body:
# Support agent overview

Harbor Notes is a fictional workspace app. This example explains how its support agent answers a customer using product documentation, with a human handoff when an answer needs review. All content is synthetic.

## Follow one question

> How do I export my workspace?

1. [[Retrieval design]] finds relevant documentation.
2. [[Answer generation]] drafts an answer from the retrieved sources.
3. [[Answer checks]] decides whether to send the answer or start a [[Human handoff]].
4. Both paths finish at Customer reply.

## Example source

| Source ID | Title | Approved content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| exports-01 | Export a workspace | Open Workspace settings, choose Export, then Download JSON. |
| exports-02 | Export contents | A JSON export contains the workspace's projects and notes. |

The normal path should answer: "Open Workspace settings, choose Export, then Download JSON. The export includes your projects and notes."

## Explore the map

Start with Retrieve knowledge, Generate answer, Check answer, and Human handoff folded. Unfold Retrieve knowledge, then Hybrid search to see the query split into semantic and keyword search.

[[Response contract]] is shared by generation, checking, and the final reply. [[Retrieval runbook]] gives a concrete example of an unsuccessful lookup.

This file describes a system. Merfolk's pulse animation illustrates its connections; the demo contains no API credentials or live integrations.

pages.title: Retrieval design
pages.body:
# Retrieval design

Owner: Knowledge team.

Retrieval turns the customer's words into ranked, attributable evidence. It keeps exact product terms while also searching for related wording.

{{diagram:Retrieval}}

## Input and output

| Boundary | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Input | Customer question and the active product version |
| Output | Ranked excerpts, stable source IDs, titles, and document versions |
| No useful result | An empty evidence list that [[Answer checks]] can identify |

## Why two search paths?

[[Hybrid search]] finds related wording through a vector index and exact terms through a keyword index. Both branches enter Merge results. Rerank evidence chooses the excerpts that best address the question.

For "How do I export my workspace?", preserve the words "export" and "workspace" and rank exports-01 above general workspace documentation.

## Failure behavior

An unavailable index or irrelevant result must stay visible to the caller. Do not invent a source to fill the gap. See [[Retrieval runbook]] for the operating steps and [[Response contract]] for the evidence fields.

Continue to [[Answer generation]] with the ranked excerpts.

pages.title: Retrieval runbook
pages.body:
# Retrieval runbook

Owner: Knowledge team.

Use this page when retrieval returns no useful evidence or an index is unavailable. Retrieve knowledge links this runbook as its second page, after [[Retrieval design]].

## Investigate

- [ ] Record the customer's question and the product version.
- [ ] Check that semantic and keyword searches used the same document version.
- [ ] Inspect both result lists before Merge results.
- [ ] Verify that Rerank evidence kept the original source IDs.
- [ ] Pass an empty evidence list to [[Answer checks]] if no excerpt answers the question.
- [ ] Follow [[Human handoff]] when an answer requires unsupported information.

## Reproduce the exception

Ask: "Can you restore a workspace that I deleted last year?"

The demo's approved sources cover exports only. They provide no restoration policy. A draft that promises restoration should fail the source check and create a support ticket.

## Recovery

Add an approved restoration article to the knowledge source, rebuild both indexes, and retry the question. A recovered search should return the new source ID and version in the [[Response contract]].

pages.title: Hybrid search
pages.body:
# Hybrid search

Owner: Search team.

Run both searches for the same rewritten question. Merge their results before reranking.

{{diagram:Search}}

| Branch | Purpose | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Embed query, then Vector index | Match related wording | "Save a copy of my workspace" can match an export article. |
| Keyword index | Preserve exact terms | "Download JSON" should match the documented command. |
| Merge results | Deduplicate by source ID | exports-01 appears once even when both branches find it. |

This group is nested inside Retrieve knowledge. Folding it preserves the incoming semantic and exact-term connections as a combined crease. Unfold it to inspect the two paths again.

Return merged candidates to [[Retrieval design]]. Keep each excerpt's provenance for [[Response contract]].

pages.title: Answer generation
pages.body:
# Answer generation

Owner: Assistant team.

Build a draft from the question, ranked excerpts, and support instructions. The draft remains subject to [[Answer checks]].

{{diagram:Generation}}

## Responsibilities

| Step | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Build context | Include the question, relevant excerpts, source IDs, and versions. |
| Apply instructions | Ask for direct steps and require a source for factual claims. |
| Draft answer | Return the proposed reply and its citations using [[Response contract]]. |

## Example draft

> Open Workspace settings, choose Export, then Download JSON. Your export includes your projects and notes.

The steps cite exports-01. The statement about contents cites exports-02. Both sources appear in [[Support agent overview]].

## Insufficient evidence

If [[Retrieval design]] finds no relevant article, return an unresolved draft with an empty citation list. Leave the unsupported question for [[Human handoff]].

pages.title: Answer checks
pages.body:
# Answer checks

Owner: Support platform team.

An answer reaches the customer automatically only when its factual claims have supporting excerpts and its proposed action follows the documented support policy.

{{diagram:Quality}}

## Decision table

| Evidence | Policy | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Citations support the answer | Action is documented | Follow yes to Customer reply. |
| A claim has no supporting excerpt | Any | Follow no to [[Human handoff]]. |
| Citations support the answer | Action needs a specialist | Follow no to [[Human handoff]]. |

Check citations first, then policy. Ready to send? combines those results. The demo animates both outgoing branches to explain the available paths; playback does not evaluate the customer's question.

## Example outcomes

"How do I export my workspace?" can follow yes using exports-01 and exports-02.

"Can you restore a workspace that I deleted last year?" follows no because the demo provides no restoration policy. See [[Retrieval runbook]].

[[Answer generation]] and this group share the same [[Response contract]] page.

pages.title: Human handoff
pages.body:
# Human handoff

Owner: Customer support team.

Create a support ticket when [[Answer checks]] cannot approve the draft. A support specialist reviews the evidence and writes the final reply.

{{diagram:Handoff}}

## Ticket contents

- The customer's original question.
- Retrieved excerpts and their source IDs.
- The proposed answer, if one exists.
- The reason automatic delivery stopped.
- The product and documentation versions.

For the restoration question, record: "The available documentation covers workspace exports. No approved restoration policy was found."

## Completion

The specialist verifies the applicable policy, responds to the customer, and adds missing documentation when appropriate. Both the automatic and reviewed paths finish at Customer reply.

This page is linked to Human handoff, Support ticket, and Support specialist. Editing it from any of those nodes changes the same page. Return to [[Support agent overview]] for the complete story.

pages.title: Response contract
pages.body:
# Response contract

Owner: Support platform team.

[[Answer generation]], [[Answer checks]], and Customer reply link this shared page. Each component uses the same meaning for a proposed answer and its sources.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| question | The customer's original words |
| answer | Proposed customer-facing text |
| citations | Source IDs and the claims they support |
| outcome | ready or needs_review |
| reason | Explanation when review is required |

## Example

```json
{
  "question": "How do I export my workspace?",
  "answer": "Open Workspace settings, choose Export, then Download JSON.",
  "citations": [
    { "source_id": "exports-01", "claim": "workspace export steps" }
  ],
  "outcome": "ready",
  "reason": ""
}
```

These are illustrative fields for the fictional support system, not Merfolk's import schema. The reimportable demo uses Merfolk's version 3 diagram format.

[[Retrieval design]] supplies the evidence. [[Human handoff]] keeps the same evidence attached when a specialist must review the request.
